metadata.description: Qwen3-8B-Base vs Qwen3-8B (thinking off) on two path-search tasks (T1 unweighted grid path, T2 weighted shortest path). Arms: base template-free, base chat-templated, instruct chat, instruct template-free (2x2), modal-ban arms, and HF steering arms that subtract the paired instruct-minus-base residual difference (band-incremental over layers 8-28, plus fallbacks). Every program is scored on >=44 hidden tests and labelled by a runtime-signature + AST labeller with a blind LLM judge for disagreements.

deviations.what: Models read from the run's shared HF cache (HF_HOME preset by the platform) instead of ./hf_cache
deviations.why: Platform rule: never override HF_HOME/TRANSFORMERS_CACHE (avoids duplicate weights); no workspace hf_cache exists

deviations.what: vLLM 0.11.0 run with enforce_eager=True, max_num_seqs=48 (plan: 16), generation_config='vllm'
deviations.why: Container has no C compiler for Triton/Inductor; max_num_seqs only changes throughput; generation_config='vllm' guarantees the HF sampling defaults (T=0.6, top_p=0.95, top_k=20) are never merged

deviations.what: Program extraction keeps only top-level imports/defs/classes/assignments for EVERY arm (plan: template-free arms only)
deviations.why: Identical rule across arms so module-level demo code (prints, example calls) can never crash an otherwise valid chat solution

deviations.what: Steering arms use a custom decode loop (Gumbel-max over full-vocab float32 logits at T=1, one CUDA generator per (task, paraphrase, sample)) instead of HF generate + torch.manual_seed per batch
deviations.why: Exact per-sample common-random-number coupling independent of batch composition (verified: hook test f2), and HF generation_config can never leak in; each batch holds 2 arms x 10 samples of one paraphrase (no padding) for ~2x throughput

deviations.what: Uniform no-code cutoff for all HF arms: a row is stopped at 512 tokens if neither ``` nor 'def solve' has appeared (finish_reason nocode_cutoff, counted as degenerate)
deviations.why: Sharpening arms produced pure garbage running to 1024 tokens; the rule is arm-blind, never fires on S0, and was applied post hoc (identically) to the 20 rows generated before it existed

deviations.what: Runtime labeller rules refined (revision rounds 1-2): IDDFS restart = >=4 waves of start-neighbour reads after reads at start-distance >=4 AND re-read ratio >=5; Bellman-Ford/SPFA from edge-list passes, edge-order sensitivity, or FIFO re-enqueues (deque and list queues) instead of exponent band [1.6,2.6)
deviations.why: The exponent band mislabels O(n^2) array Dijkstra as Bellman-Ford and the first wave rule fired on level-synchronous BFS; array-scan Dijkstra and Dial stay 'unknown' at runtime by design and are resolved by AST/judge

deviations.what: AST labeller: added level-synchronous BFS (frontier lists swapped each round) and made the Floyd-Warshall X[i][k]+X[k][j] pattern require three distinct named indices
deviations.why: Gate failures on a level-BFS variant and a false FW hit on pf[0][0]+pb[0][0] in bidirectional Dijkstra

deviations.what: Blind judge (google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite) labels every distinct parseable program, not only disagreements; the FINAL label still follows the plan rule (runtime==AST catalogue label, else judge)
deviations.why: Cost ~$0.0001/call; gives a full-sample judge-label sensitivity analysis and agreement rates per arm in addition to the 15-per-arm audit

deviations.what: Judge 'other:<sub>' labels that name a catalogue algorithm (e.g. buggy_bfs, incorrect_dijkstra_attempt) are canonicalised to that algorithm, arm-blind
deviations.why: The judge was instructed to label buggy programs by the algorithm they attempt but sometimes emitted other:buggy_X

deviations.what: PREDICT primary predictor = base_tf all parseable labelled samples restricted to survivors (fallback 3), with the correct-only version committed as first secondary
deviations.why: Only 12 (T1) and 18 (T2) correct base_tf samples (<40 per task); decided and hash-committed before phase C was sampled

deviations.what: Ban prompts use the ban sentence itself as the lead-in segment (SEG = B_i), no neutral lead-in
deviations.why: Literal reading of STEP 2.2-2.3 (SEG + spec); identical across base and instruct ban arms

deviations.what: Neutral segments P10..P49 built from 10 opener templates x 8 object phrases (P0..P9 verbatim from the plan)
deviations.why: Plan allows hand-written or template-built segments; all pass the lexicon check

deviations.what: Checkers: T1 accepts any list/tuple of 2-element int sequences; T2 accepts a numeric value equal to the expected int (e.g. 5.0)
deviations.why: Output-format leniency so correctness reflects the algorithm, not int-vs-float typing

deviations.what: Programs that time out while 5 harness workers run in parallel are re-scored once with 2 workers
deviations.why: Guards against CPU-contention false timeouts (limit floor 1 s, 10x reference)

deviations.what: Hook unit test (b) uses a relative tolerance (||err||/||delta_8|| < 2%) instead of atol 1e-2
deviations.why: Residual magnitudes are O(10-100) in bf16, so an absolute 1e-2 tolerance is below bf16 resolution; observed rel. error 0.26%

deviations.what: S3 (c=1.5) run at N=100 per task (plan: N=30 once S2 is destructive)
deviations.why: Paired batching with S1 made it free; S3 is reported as destructive

deviations.what: Sharpening knob destructive at every c (0 parseable programs at c=0.5/1.0/1.5): c* set to 0.5 (flagged); fallback-6 single-layer arms (delta_18 at layer 18, c in {0.25,0.5,1.0}, N=50/task) run; extension arms added: R-only sharpening (prefill subtraction at R only, c=1.0, N=100/task) with a norm-matched R-only random control
deviations.why: Plan fallback 6; the R-only ablation isolates the read-state claim from the destruction caused by subtracting the R-estimate at generated positions (cos(delta_R, delta_gen) only 0.15-0.42 in the band)

deviations.what: A1 (base_tf baseline) and A2 (base_chat baseline) extended from N=200/100 to N=300 per task (new seeds, appended after phase C, rows tagged stage ext_*)
deviations.why: Correct base programs were too few for the Hill_cc contrast (12-23 per task); fallback 3 allows A1 -> 300, A2 extended for the primary weights contrast; verdicts at the planned N are reported as a sensitivity (both MIXED)

deviations.what: Cutoff-validation arm: R-only sharpening (c=1.0) re-run on 20 coupled samples per task without the 512-token no-code rule (max 1024 tokens)
deviations.why: The R-only arm switches to thinking-style prose, so the uniform no-code rule could understate its parse rate; reported side by side (parse 0.30->0.55 T1, 0.15->0.40 T2; algorithm unchanged)

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows, cols = (len(grid), len(grid[0]))
    directions = ((-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1))
    path = []

    def dfs(r, c, visited):
        if (r, c) == goal:
            return True
        visited.add((r, c))
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = (r + dr, c + dc)
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols and ((nr, nc) not in visited) and (grid[nr][nc] == '.'):
                path.append((nr, nc))
                if dfs(nr, nc, visited):
                    return True
                path.pop()
        visited.remove((r, c))
        return False
    if dfs(*start, set([start])):
        return path
    return []

from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    directions = [(0, 1), (1, 0), (0, -1), (-1, 0)]

    def is_valid(x, y):
        return 0 <= x < rows and 0 <= y < cols and grid[x][y] == '.'

    queue = deque([(x, y, []) for x, y in start])
    while queue:
        x, y, path = queue.popleft()
        if (x, y) == goal:
            return path + [(x, y)]
        for dx, dy in directions:
            nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
            if is_valid(nx, ny) and (nx, ny) not in path:
                queue.append((nx, ny, path + [(x, y)]))
    return []

def move_exists(neighbors, grid):
    """This function returns the neighbors of start cell that exist in the grid"""
    (n_r, n_c) = neighbors.shape
    neighbors = list(zip(neighbors.ravel('F').tolist()))

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    """
    Returns a list of tuples containing the shortest path to reach goal from start cell
    
    Parameters:
    grid: list of free and wall cells
    start: (r, c) tuple of the start cell containing a free cell
    goal: (r, c) tuple of the goal cell containing a free cell
    """
    (sr, sc) = start
    (gr, gc) = goal

    # Convert the grid into a numpy matrix for easier indexing
    grid = np.array([[c for c in r] for r in grid])
    n_r, n_c = grid.shape
    
    # Check if start or goal is a wall cell
    if grid[sr, sc].find("#") != -1 or grid[gr, gc].find("#") != -1:
        return []
    
    # Create a queue and add the start cell
    queue = deque([(sr, sc)])
    
    # Create a dictionary to store the path from start cell to reach the current cell
    path = {start: None}
    
    # Explore the cells in the grid
    while queue:
        r, c = queue.popleft()
        if (r, c) == goal:  # Reached goal cell
            break
        
        # Find neighbors of the current cell that exist in the grid
        neighbors = np.array([[r-1, c], [r+1, c], [r, c-1], [r, c+1]])
        for neighbor in move_exists(neighbors, grid):
            if neighbor not in path:  # If the neighbor hasn't been visited
                path[neighbor] = (r, c)  # Add neighbor to the path
                queue.append(neighbor)  # Add neighbor to the queue to explore further
                continue
    
    # If goal cell wasn't reached, return an empty list
    if (gr, gc) not in path:
        return []
    
    # Create a list of cells forming the shortest path from start to goal cell
    shortest_path = []
    cell = goal
    while cell:
        shortest_path.append(cell)
        cell = path[cell]
    
    return shortest_path[::-1]

    for pair in neighbors:

            yield (r, c)

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    """
    Returns a list of tuples containing the shortest path to reach goal from start cell
    
    Parameters:
    grid: list of free and wall cells
    start: (r, c) tuple of the start cell containing a free cell
    goal: (r, c) tuple of the goal cell containing a free cell

    sr, sc = start
    gr, gc = goal
    grid = np.array([[c for c in r] for r in grid])
    n_r, n_c = grid.shape
    if grid[sr, sc].find('#') != -1 or grid[gr, gc].find('#') != -1:
        return []
    queue = deque([(sr, sc)])
    path = {start: None}
    while queue:
        r, c = queue.popleft()
        if (r, c) == goal:
            break
        neighbors = np.array([[r - 1, c], [r + 1, c], [r, c - 1], [r, c + 1]])
        for neighbor in move_exists(neighbors, grid):
            if neighbor not in path:
                path[neighbor] = (r, c)
                queue.append(neighbor)
                continue
    if (gr, gc) not in path:
        return []
    shortest_path = []
    cell = goal
    while cell:
        shortest_path.append(cell)
        cell = path[cell]
    return shortest_path[::-1]

from itertools import tee # <- iterator module

def solve(grid, start, goal, path=None):
    # work directly on grid characters in-place,
    # to avoid unnecessary copying. "#\0"
    # means "this cell is visited"
    # Thanks to tjungbluth and Ayman Jaroudi
    i, j = start
    path = path or [start]
    grid[i] = grid[i][:j] + "\0" + grid[i][j + 1:]
    if goal == path[0]:
        return path
    for ii, jj in ((i, j - 1), (i - 1, j), (i, j + 1), (i + 1, j)):
        if ii >= 0 and ii < len(grid) and \
           jj >= 0 and jj < len(grid[0]) and \
           grid[ii][jj] in '.\0':
            sp = solve(grid, (ii, jj), goal, path)
            if sp is not None:
                return sp
    return None

def solve(grid, start, goal):

            from start to goal, including both ends. If goal cannot be

    if not (0 <= start[0] < len(grid)) or not (0 <= start[1] < len(grid[0])):
        raise ValueError("Invalid start position")
    if not (0 <= goal[0] < len(grid)) or not (0 <= goal[1] < len(grid[0])):
        raise ValueError("Invalid goal position")

    # Ensure both start and goal are free cells
    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] != '.' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] != '.':
        return []

    # Define the four possible moves (up, down, left, right)
    moves = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]

    # Initialize BFS parameters
    queue = deque([(start, [start])])  # queue of (current cell, path)
    visited = set()  # set of visited cells

    while queue:
        current, path = queue.popleft()

        # If the current cell is the goal, return the current path
        if current == goal:
            return path

        # Otherwise, explore all adjacent free cells
        for move in moves:
            new_row, new_col = current[0] + move[0], current[1] + move[1]

            # Check if the new cell is within bounds and not a wall
            if (

                if (new_row, new_col) not in visited:
                    visited.add((new_row, new_col))
                    queue.append(((new_row, new_col), path + [(new_row, new_col)]))

    # Returns an empty list if no path is found
    return []

    area = [(H, G, heuristic(H, G))]

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    """
    Finds a path from the start to the goal in the grid.

    Parameters:
    - grid: List of strings representing the grid, with '.' for free cells and '#' for walls.
    - start: Tuple of (row, col) for the start cell.
    - goal: Tuple of (row, col) for the goal cell.

    Returns:
    - List of (row, col) tuples representing the path from start to goal, including both ends.
      Returns an empty list if no path exists.
    """
    # Helper function to check if a cell is within the grid
    def in_bounds(pos):
        row, col = pos
        return 0 <= row < len(grid) and 0 <= col < len(grid[0]) and grid[row][col] == '.'

    # Helper function to get valid neighbors from a cell
    def get_neighbors(pos):
        row, col = pos
        for dr, dc in [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]:
            neighbor = (row + dr, col + dc)
            if in_bounds(neighbor):
                yield neighbor

    # Priority queue for A* algorithm
    queue = [(0, start)]
    came_from = {start: None}
    cost_so_far = {start: 0}

    while queue:
        _, current = heapq.heappop(queue)

        if current == goal:
            # Reconstruct path
            path = []
            while current:
                path.append(current)
                current = came_from[current]
            return path[::-1]  # Return reversed path from start to goal

        for next in get_neighbors(current):
            new_cost = cost_so_far[current] + 1
            if next not in cost_so_far or new_cost < cost_so_far[next]:
                cost_so_far[next] = new_cost
                priority = new_cost + heuristic(next, goal)
                heapq.heappush(queue, (priority, next))
                came_from[next] = current

    return []  # No path found

# Helper function for heuristic (Manhattan distance)
def heuristic(a, b):
    return abs(a[0] - b[0]) + abs(a[1] - b[1])

    def arc_consistency(self, queue=None):
        """
        INPUT:

        queue = queue or list(self.constraints.keys())
        in_queue = dict((arc, False) for arc in queue)

        revised = False

        def find_shortest_route(route_map, start, end):
                """
                Finds the shortest route between two points using Dijkstra's Algorithm.

                Args:
                        route_map (list of strings): Each string represents a row in the "map".
                                                        Use "." for accessible cells and "#" for walls.
                        start (tuple): The starting position (row, col) as x-index and y-index in route_map. 
                        end (tuple): The destination position (row, col) as x-index and y-index in route_map. 

                Returns:
                        list of tuples: A connected list of coordinates [(x1, y1), (x2, y2), ...] 
                                        from start position to the end position, 
                                        representing the shortest route, 
                                        including both start and end position.
                        An empty list if there is no accessible route.
                """
                import heapq

                m, n = len(route_map), len(route_map[0])
                directions = [(1,0), (0,1), (-1,0), (0,-1)]

                def is_within_boundaries(i, j):
                        return 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n

                def coordinate_to_index(current_row, current_col):
                        return current_row*n + current_col

                def index_to_coordinate(index):
                        return (index//n, index%n)

                def get_neighboring_cells(current_row, current_col):
                        for dx, dy in directions:
                                new_row, new_col = current_row+dx, current_col+dy

                                if not is_within_boundaries(new_row, new_col):
                                        continue

                                if route_map[new_row][new_col] == "#":
                                        continue

                                yield new_row, new_col

                dist = [[float("inf")]*n for _ in range(m)]
                prev = [[-1]*n for _ in range(m)]

                dist[start[0]][start[1]] = 0

                # use (distance, current_row, current_col) as the priority for heap
                heap = [(0, start[0], start[1])]
                
                while heap:
                        dist_now, cur_row, cur_col = heapq.heappop(heap)
                        index_now = coordinate_to_index(cur_row, cur_col)
                        
                        if dist_now > dist[cur_row][cur_col]:
                                continue

                        if (cur_row, cur_col) == end:
                                break

                        for new_row, new_col in get_neighboring_cells(cur_row, cur_col):
                                new_index = coordinate_to_index(new_row, new_col)
                                new_dist = dist_now + 1

                                if new_dist < dist[new_row][new_col]:
                                        dist[new_row][new_col] = new_dist
                                        prev[new_row][new_col] = index_now
                                        heapq.heappush(heap, (new_dist, new_row, new_col))

                        route_coordinates.append(index_to_coordinate(current_index))

from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    # Parse grid size
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    
    # Check if start or goal is not on the grid or not free
    if (grid[start[0]][start[1]] != '.' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] != '.') or \
       (start[0] < 0 or start[0] >= rows or start[1] < 0 or start[1] >= cols) or \
       (goal[0] < 0 or goal[0] >= rows or goal[1] < 0 or goal[1] >= cols):
        return []
    
    # Define directions (up, down, left, right)
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    
    # Initialize BFS queue with start position and an empty path
    queue = deque([([start], start)])
    
    while queue:
        path, current = queue.popleft()
        
        # If reached goal, return path
        if current == goal:
            return path + [current]
        
        # Explore neighbors
        for dx, dy in directions:
            nx, ny = current[0] + dx, current[1] + dy
            if 0 <= nx < rows and 0 <= ny < cols and grid[nx][ny] == '.':
                queue.append((path + [current], (nx, ny)))
    
    # If no path found, return empty list
    return []

from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    directions = [(0, 1), (0, -1), (1, 0), (-1, 0)]

    def inside(x, y):
        return 0 <= x < rows and 0 <= y < cols and grid[x][y] == '.'

    visited = set([start])
    queue = deque([[start]])

    while queue:
        path = queue.popleft()
        x, y = path[-1]
        if (x, y) == goal:
            return path

        for dx, dy in directions:
            nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
            if inside(nx, ny) and (nx, ny) not in visited:
                visited.add((nx, ny))
                queue.append(path + [(nx, ny)])

    return []

5. **Goal Reached**:

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    # Define possible moves (up, down, left, right)
    moves = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    
    # Convert grid to a more convenient representation (list of lists)
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    grid_map = [[cell == '.' for cell in row] for row in grid]
    
    # Check if start and goal are valid
    if not (0 <= start[0] < rows and 0 <= start[1] < cols and grid_map[start[0]][start[1]]):
        return []
    if not (0 <= goal[0] < rows and 0 <= goal[1] < cols and grid_map[goal[0]][goal[1]]):
        return []
    
    # BFS queue
    queue = deque([(start, [start])])
    
    # Visited set
    visited = set([start])
    
    while queue:
        (current, path) = queue.popleft()
        
        if current == goal:
            # Convert coordinates back to original format
            solution = [(c[0], c[1]) for c in path]
            return solution

            if (0 <= next_cell[0] < rows and 
                0 <= next_cell[1] < cols and 
                grid_map[next_cell[0]][next_cell[1]] and 
                next_cell not in visited):
                visited.add(next_cell)
                queue.append((next_cell, path + [next_cell]))
    
    # If no path is found, return an empty list

class Solution:
    def solve(self, grid: List[str], start: List[int], goal: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        # Add protection against invalid start/goal
        if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
            raise ValueError('Start or goal points are in a wall.')
        
        R, C = len(grid), len(grid[0])
        directions = [(1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)]
        
        # Convert start & goal to coordinates
        start_coords = (start[0] * C + start[1], start[1])
        goal_coords = (goal[0] * C + goal[1], goal[1])
        
        # Create adjacency list
        adj_list = defaultdict(list)
        for r in range(R):
            for c in range(C):
                if grid[r][c] == '.':
                    node = r * C + c
                    for dr, dc in directions:
                        new_r, new_c = r + dr, c + dc
                        if 0 <= new_r < R and 0 <= new_c < C and grid[new_r][new_c] == '.':
                            adj_list[node].append(new_c - c)
                            adj_list[node + C * (new_r - r)].append(-c + new_c)

        def dijkstra(start):
            distances = defaultdict(lambda: float('inf'))
            distances[start] = 0
            pq = [(0, start)]
            while pq:
                curr_dist, curr_node = heapq.heappop(pq)
                if curr_node == goal_coords: return curr_dist
                if curr_dist > distances[curr_node]: continue
                for neighbor in adj_list[curr_node]:
                    new_dist = curr_dist + (1 if neighbor < 0 else 0)
                    if new_dist < distances[neighbor]:
                        distances[neighbor] = new_dist
                        heapq.heappush(pq, (new_dist, neighbor))
            return -1
        
        dist = dijkstra(start_coords)
        return [[r, c] for r, c in [(r // C, r % C) for r in range(R * C) if r == start_coords or (r - dist) in adj_list]]

import collections

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    # Convert grid to a 2D list of integers where 0 represents a free cell and 1 represents a wall
    grid_int = [[1 if cell == '#' else 0 for cell in row] for row in grid]
    
    # Initialize the directions for moving up, down, left, or right
    directions = [(0, 1), (0, -1), (1, 0), (-1, 0)]
    
    # Initialize the queue with the starting position and an empty path
    queue = collections.deque([(start, [start])])
    
    # Initialize a set of visited positions
    visited = set()
    visited.add(start)
    
    # Loop until the queue is empty
    while queue:
        # Dequeue the current position and path
        position, path = queue.popleft()
        
        # If the current position is the goal, return the path
        if position == goal:
            return path
        
        # Get the row and column of the current position
        row, col = position
        
        # Get the value of the current cell
        cell_value = grid_int[row][col]
        
        # If the cell is a wall, skip it
        if cell_value == 1:
            continue
        
        # Iterate over the directions
        for direction in directions:
            # Get the new row and column
            new_row, new_col = row + direction[0], col + direction[1]
            
            # If the new position is outside the grid, skip it
            if new_row < 0 or new_row >= len(grid) or new_col < 0 or new_col >= len(grid[0]):
                continue
            
            # If the new position has not been visited or discovered as a wall, enqueue it
            if grid_int[new_row][new_col] == 0 and (new_row, new_col) not in visited:
                visited.add((new_row, new_col))
                queue.append(((new_row, new_col), path + [(new_row, new_col)]))
    
    # If the queue is empty and the goal has not been reached, return an empty list
    return []

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    """
    A function that takes a grid, start, and goal as input parameters and returns a list of tuples
    representing a path from start to goal within the grid. If no path exists, an empty list is returned.

    The function uses the A* algorithm to find the shortest path from start to goal.
    """
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])

    # Helper function to get the neighbors of a cell
    def get_neighbors(row, col):
        neighbors = []
        if row > 0:
            neighbors.append((row-1, col))
        if row < rows-1:
            neighbors.append((row+1, col))
        if col > 0:
            neighbors.append((row, col-1))
        if col < cols-1:
            neighbors.append((row, col+1))
        return neighbors

    # Helper function to calculate the cost of a path
    def cost(path):
        return len(path)

    # Initialize the open and closed lists
    open_list = []
    closed_list = set()

    # Add the start state to the open list
    heapq.heappush(open_list, (0, [start]))

    # Loop until we find the goal state or the open list is empty
    while open_list:
        # Get the current state with the lowest cost
        cost_so_far, current_path = heapq.heappop(open_list)

        # Get the current state from the path
        current_state = current_path[-1]

        # Check if the current state is the goal state
        if current_state == goal:
            return current_path

        # Add the current state to the closed list
        closed_list.add(current_state)

        # Get the neighbors of the current state
        neighbors = get_neighbors(*current_state)

        # Add each neighbor to the open list if it is not in the closed list
        for neighbor in neighbors:
            if neighbor not in closed_list:
                new_path = current_path + [neighbor]
                # Calculate the cost of the new path
                new_cost = cost(new_path)
                if (new_cost, new_path) not in open_list:
                    heapq.heappush(open_list, (new_cost, new_path))
    # If we reach this point, the goal state is not reachable
    return []

    Parameters
    ----------

    start : tuple (int, int)
        The starting position (row, col) in the grid.

    list of tuples
        A list of positions (row, col) forming a valid path from start to goal.
    """

    grid = [list(row) for row in grid]

    directions = [(0, 1), (0, -1), (1, 0), (-1, 0)]

    def is_valid(pos):
        row, col = pos
        return (0 <= row < len(grid)) and (0 <= col < len(grid[0])) and grid[row][col] == '.'

    # Initialize a queue for BFS and a visited set to track visited positions
    queue = [start]
    visited = set([start])

    # Initialize the path dictionary to track the path
    path = {start: None}

import heapq

# General priority queue class
class PriorityQueue:
    def __init__(self):
        self.elements = []

    def empty(self):
        return len(self.elements) == 0

    def put(self, item, priority):
        heapq.heappush(self.elements, (priority, item))

    def get(self):
        return heapq.heappop(self.elements)[1]

# Euclidean distance heuristic function
def heuristic(a, b):
    return ((b[0] - a[0]) ** 2 + (b[1] - a[1]) ** 2) ** 0.5

# A* search algorithm
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    # Define the grid dimensions
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0]) if rows else 0

    # Check if start and goal are within the grid
    if not (0 <= start[0] < rows and 0 <= start[1] < cols):
        return []
    if not (0 <= goal[0] < rows and 0 <= goal[1] < cols):
        return []

    # Check if start or goal is a wall
    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#':
        return []
    if grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []

    # Initialize the priority queue
    frontier = PriorityQueue()
    frontier.put(start, 0)

    # Create a dictionary to keep track of the cost to reach each node
    came_from = {}
    came_from[start] = None

    # Create a dictionary to keep track of the cost to reach each node
    cost_so_far = {}
    cost_so_far[start] = 0

    # Directions: up, down, left, right
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]

    while not frontier.empty():
        current = frontier.get()

        if current == goal:
            # Reconstruct the path
            path = []
            while current is not None:
                path.append(current)
                current = came_from[current]
            return path[::-1]

        for direction in directions:
            next_cell = (current[0] + direction[0], current[1] + direction[1])

            # Check if the next cell is within the grid
            if (0 <= next_cell[0] < rows and 0 <= next_cell[1] < cols):
                # Check if the next cell is a wall
                if grid[next_cell[0]][next_cell[1]] == '#':
                    continue

                # Calculate the new cost
                new_cost = cost_so_far[current] + 1

                if next_cell not in cost_so_far or new_cost < cost_so_far[next_cell]:
                    cost_so_far[next_cell] = new_cost
                    priority = new_cost + heuristic(goal, next_cell)
                    frontier.put(next_cell, priority)
                    came_from[next_cell] = current

    return []

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    """

    Parameters:
    - grid: A list of equal-length strings representing the grid.
    - start: A tuple (row, col) of the starting cell.

    - A list of (row, col) tuples forming a valid path from start to goal.
    - If no path exists, returns an empty list.

    # Initialize the queue with the starting position and the path so far
    queue = deque([(start, [start])])
    
    # Get the dimensions of the grid
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    
    # Define the possible moves (up, down, left, right)
    moves = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    
    while queue:
        ((row, col), path) = queue.popleft()
        
        # Check if the current cell is the goal
        if (row, col) == goal:

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    """Return a list of (row, col) tuples forming a valid path from start to goal.
    
    Args:
        grid: A list of equal-length strings, where '.' is a free cell and '#' is a wall.
        start: A tuple (row, col) representing the starting cell.
        goal: A tuple (row, col) representing the goal cell.
    
    Returns:
        A list of (row, col) tuples forming a valid path from start to goal, or an empty list if the goal cannot be reached.
    """
    def is_valid_cell(r, c):
        """Check if the cell (r, c) is within the grid and is a free cell."""
        return 0 <= r < len(grid) and 0 <= c < len(grid[0]) and grid[r][c] == '.'
    
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    
    # Directions for moving up, down, left, right
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    
    # BFS initialization
    from collections import deque
    
    queue = deque([(start, [start])])
    visited = set([start])
    
    while queue:
        (current_row, current_col), path = queue.popleft()
        
        # If we reached the goal, return the path
        if (current_row, current_col) == goal:
            return path
        
        # Explore all possible moves
        for dr, dc in directions:
            new_row, new_col = current_row + dr, current_col + dc
            
            if is_valid_cell(new_row, new_col) and (new_row, new_col) not in visited:
                visited.add((new_row, new_col))
                queue.append(((new_row, new_col), path + [(new_row, new_col)]))
    
    # If no path found, return an empty list
    return []
```

This function uses Breadth-First Search (BFS) to find a path from the `start` cell to the `goal` cell in the `grid`. The BFS ensures that we explore all possible paths level by level, guaranteeing that if a path exists, it will be found.

``` The problem is asking us to find a path from a start point to a goal point in a grid, avoiding walls, and returning the path as a list of (row, col) tuples.

Here's a solution in Python:

```python
    def solve(self, b):     # Assume that b is a list of strings representing the grid

        def bfs(start, goal):
            # Initialize the queue with the start position
            queue = [b[start[0]][start[1]]]
            # Initialize the path with the start position
            path = [start]
            # While there are still positions to check in the queue
            while queue:
                # Take the next position from the queue
                current = queue.pop(0)
                # If the current position is the goal
                if current == goal:
                    # Return the path to the goal
                    return path
                # Otherwise, add the neighboring positions to the queue
                for neighbor in [(0, 1), (1, 0), (0, -1), (-1, 0)]:
                    row, col = current[0] + neighbor[0], current[1] + neighbor[1]
                    # If the neighbor is within the bounds of the grid and not a wall
                    if row >= 0 and row < len(b) and col >= 0 and col < len(b[0]) and b[row][col] == '.':
                        # Add the neighbor to the path and the queue
                        path.append((row, col))
                        queue.append((row, col))
                        # Set the neighbor to be a wall to prevent revisiting
                        b[row][col] = '#'
            # If we exhaust the queue without finding the goal, return an empty list
            return []

        # Convert the grid from a list of strings to a list of lists of characters
        b = [list(row) for row in b]
        # Find the start and goal positions
        start = next((i, j) for i, row in enumerate(b) for j, cell in enumerate(row) if cell == '.')
        goal = next((i, j) for i, row in enumerate(b) for j, cell in enumerate(row) if cell == '.')
        # Return the path from the start to the goal
        return bfs(start, goal)
```

### Explanation:
- The `solve` function takes a grid `b` as input, which is a list of strings.
- The `bfs` helper function performs a breadth-first search (BFS) to find a path from the start to the goal.
- The `bfs` function initializes a queue with the start position and a path with the start position.
- The BFS loop continues until the queue is empty or the goal is found.
- Inside the loop, the `bfs` function checks the neighboring positions (up, down, left, right) of the current position.
- If a neighboring position is within the bounds of the grid, not a wall, and empty, it is added to the path and the queue.
- The neighboring position is then set to a wall to prevent revisiting.
- If the goal is found, the path is returned.
- If the BFS loop exhausts the queue without finding the goal, an empty list is returned.
- The `solve` function converts the grid from a list of strings to a list of lists of characters for easier manipulation.
- The `solve` function finds the start and goal positions and calls the `bfs` function with these positions.
- The `solve` function returns the path from the start to the goal. ```

    """
    Solves the grid navigation problem by finding a path from start to goal.
    Returns a list of (row, col) tuples forming a valid path, including both ends.
    If the goal cannot be reached, returns an empty list.
    """
    max_rows = len(grid)
    max_cols = len(grid[0])
    visited = [[False for _ in range(max_cols)] for _ in range(max_rows)]
    stack = [(start[0], start[1])]
    
    while stack:
        current_row, current_col = stack.pop()
        if not is_valid_move(grid, current_row, current_col, max_rows, max_cols) or visited[current_row][current_col]:

        visited[current_row][current_col] = True
        
        if (current_row, current_col) == goal:
            path = []
            while current_row != start[0] or current_col != start[1]:
                path.append((current_row, current_col))
                # Deduction logic based on the last operation
                if current_row < start[0]:

                elif current_row > start[0]:

        stack.append((current_row, current_col - 1))

def solve(grid, start, goal):

    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]

    # Initialize the queue with the start position and its path
    queue = [(start, [start])]

        # Mark the current position as visited
        visited.add((current_row, current_col))

        # Explore the neighbors of the current position
        for direction in directions:

- It initializes queue with the start cell and initializes visited set to keep track of cells already visited.
- While queue is not empty, it pops the first node from the queue, checks whether it's the goal cell. If it is, we build the path as list of (row, col) tuples and returns the path. If not, it generates all valid moves and adds them to the queue and the visited set.

from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    # Check if start or goal is a wall
    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []

    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    queue = deque([start])
    visited = set()
    parents = {start: None}

    while queue:
        current = queue.popleft()
        if current == goal:
            # Construct the path from start to goal
            path = []
            while current is not None:
                path.append(current)
                current = parents[current]
            return list(reversed(path))

        for dr, dc in [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]:
            r, c = current[0] + dr, current[1] + dc

            if (0 <= r < rows and 
                0 <= c < cols and 
                grid[r][c] != '#' and 
                (r, c) not in visited):
                
                visited.add((r, c))
                parents[(r, c)] = current
                queue.append((r, c))

    # If there's no path
    return []

    queue = deque([(start, [start])])

def solve(grid: list[str], start: tuple[int, int], goal: tuple[int, int]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """
    Solves the grid path problem using Breadth-First Search (BFS) to find the path from start to goal.
    
    :param grid: List of equal-length strings representing the grid, where '.'
                 represents a free cell and '#' represents a wall.
    :param start: Tuple (row, col) of the starting cell.
    :param goal: Tuple (row, col) of the goal cell.
    :return: A list of (row, col) tuples forming a valid path from start to goal,
             including both ends. If goal cannot be reached, return an empty list.
    """

    # Directions for moving (up, down, left, right)
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]

    # Number of rows and columns in the grid
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    # Queue for BFS (row, col, path)
    queue = [([list(row) for row in grid], start[0], start[1], [start])]
    
    # Visited set to avoid reprocessing the same cell multiple times
    visited = set()

    while queue:
        current_grid, current_row, current_col, path = queue.pop(0)
        
        # If the current cell is the goal, return the path
        if (current_row, current_col) == goal:
            return path
        
        # Check all four possible movements
        for dr, dc in directions:
            new_row, new_col = current_row + dr, current_col + dc
            
            # Check bounds and ensure the cell is free
            if (0 <= new_row < rows and 0 <= new_col < cols and
                current_grid[new_row][new_col] == '.'):
                
                # Create a copy of the current grid and mark the cell as visited
                new_grid = [list(row) for row in current_grid]
                new_grid[new_row][new_col] = '#'  # Marking visited cell
                new_grid_tup = tuple(tuple(row) for row in new_grid)
                
                # Ensure we haven't visited this configuration before
                if (new_grid_tup, new_row, new_col) not in visited:
                    visited.add((new_grid_tup, new_row, new_col))
                    # Enqueue the new state
                    queue.append((new_grid, new_row, new_col, path + [(new_row, new_col)]))
    
    # If the goal is not reachable, return an empty list
    return []

from collections import deque

def is_valid_move(grid, row, col):
    return 0 <= row < len(grid) and 0 <= col < len(grid[0]) and grid[row][col] == \'.\'


def get_neighbors(grid, row, col):
    moves = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]  # up, down, left, right
    neighbors = []
    for dx, dy in moves:
        new_row, new_col = row + dy, col + dx
        if is_valid_move(grid, new_row, new_col):
            neighbors.append((new_row, new_col))
    return neighbors


def solve(grid, start, goal):
    if not is_valid_move(grid, *start) or not is_valid_move(grid, *goal):
        return []
    
    queue = deque([(start, [start])])
    while queue:
        (cur_row, cur_col), path = queue.popleft()
        if (cur_row, cur_col) == goal:
            return path
        # Push all neighbors onto the queue
        for neighbor in get_neighbors(grid, cur_row, cur_col):
            queue.append((neighbor, path + [neighbor]))
    
    return []  # If no path is found, return an empty list

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    # Precompute the rows and cols
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0]) if rows > 0 else 0
    
    # Possible moves: up, down, left, right
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    
    # Check if the start or goal is out of bounds or a wall
    if (start[0] < 0 or start[0] >= rows or
        start[1] < 0 or start[1] >= cols or

        goal[1] < 0 or goal[1] >= cols or
        grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#'):
        return []
    
    # Initialize the BFS queue with the start position
    queue = deque([start])
    
    # Dictionary to keep track of the path
    came_from = {start: None}
    
    while queue:
        current = queue.popleft()
        
        # Check if we have reached the goal
        if current == goal:
            # Reconstruct the path
            path = []
            while current:
                path.append(current)
                current = came_from[current]
            return path[::-1]
        
        # Explore all possible moves
        for direction in directions:

                0 <= neighbor[1] < cols and
                grid[neighbor[0]][neighbor[1]] == '.'):

                    queue.append(neighbor)
                    came_from[neighbor] = current

from typing import List, Tuple

def solve(grid: List[str], start: Tuple[int, int], goal: Tuple[int, int]) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
    # Initialize a queue for BFS
    queue = [start]
    # Initialize a visited set to avoid revisiting nodes
    visited = set()
    # Initialize a parent dictionary to reconstruct the path
    parent = {}

    # Convert the grid into a 2D list of characters for easier access
    grid = [list(row) for row in grid]

    # Get the dimensions of the grid
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])

    # Define the directions for moving up, down, left, and right
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]

    while queue:
        current = queue.pop(0)
        if current == goal:
            # Reconstruct the path from start to goal
            path = []
            while current != start:
                path.append(current)
                current = parent[current]
            path.append(start)
            path.reverse()
            return path

        # Mark the current cell as visited
        visited.add(current)

        # Explore all four directions
        for direction in directions:
            next_row = current[0] + direction[0]
            next_col = current[1] + direction[1]

            # Check if the next cell is within the grid and is a free cell
            if 0 <= next_row < rows and 0 <= next_col < cols and grid[next_row][next_col] == '.' and (next_row, next_col) not in visited:
                queue.append((next_row, next_col))
                visited.add((next_row, next_col))
                parent[(next_row, next_col)] = current

    # If the goal is not reachable, return an empty list
    return []

def is_valid_move(grid, current_row, current_col):
    return 0 <= current_row < len(grid) and 0 <= current_col < len(grid[0]) and grid[current_row][current_col] == '.'

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    # Directions for moving up, down, left, and right
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    
    # Queue for BFS: stores (current position, path so far)
    queue = deque([(start, [start])])
    
    while queue:
        ((current_row, current_col), path) = queue.popleft()
        
        # Check if we've reached the goal
        if (current_row, current_col) == goal:
            return path
        
        # Explore all valid neighbors
        for row_change, col_change in directions:
            new_row, new_col = current_row + row_change, current_col + col_change
            
            if is_valid_move(grid, new_row, new_col):
                queue.append(((new_row, new_col), path + [(new_row, new_col)]))

My solution was motivated by the problem statement, which explicitly requests a shortest path. All other solutions I had in mind would return some path, but not necessarily the shortest one. def solve(grid, start, goal):
    def dfs(row, col, path, visited):
        if (row, col) == goal:
            return path
        n = len(grid)
        m = len(grid[0])
        if (row < 0 or row >= n or col < 0 or col >= m or
            grid[row][col] == '#' or visited[row][col]):

        visited[row][col] = True
        neighbors = [[0, 1], [0, -1], [1, 0], [-1, 0]]

    m = len(grid[0])
    visited = [[False] * m for _ in range(n)]
    return dfs(start[0], start[1], [start], visited)

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    from collections import deque
    
    def is_valid_move(row, col):
        return 0 <= row < len(grid) and 0 <= col < len(grid[0]) and grid[row][col] == '.'
    
    def get_neighbors(row, col):
        neighbors = []
        for dr, dc in [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]:
            nr, nc = row + dr, col + dc
            if is_valid_move(nr, nc):
                neighbors.append((nr, nc))
        return neighbors
    
    queue = deque([(start, [start])])
    visited = set()
    visited.add(start)
    
    while queue:
        (row, col), path = queue.popleft()
        if (row, col) == goal:
            return path
        
        for neighbor in get_neighbors(row, col):
            if neighbor not in visited:
                visited.add(neighbor)
                queue.append((neighbor, path + [neighbor]))
    
    return []

import heapq
from typing import List, Tuple

def solve(grid: List[str], start: Tuple[int, int], goal: Tuple[int, int]) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
    # Parse grid
    height = len(grid)
    width = len(grid[0])
    start_row, start_col = start
    goal_row, goal_col = goal
    
    # Initialize distance grid and priority queue
    distances = [[float('inf')] * width for _ in range(height)]
    distances[start_row][start_col] = 0
    heap = [(0, start_row, start_col)]
    
    # Define possible moves (up, down, left, right)
    moves = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    
    while heap:
        dist, row, col = heapq.heappop(heap)
        
        # Check if we have reached the goal
        if (row, col) == (goal_row, goal_col):
            break
        
        # Skip if current distance is not the shortest known so far
        if dist > distances[row][col]:
            continue
        
        for move in moves:
            newRow, newCol = row + move[0], col + move[1]
            
            # Check if the new position is within the grid boundaries
            if not (0 <= newRow < height and 0 <= newCol < width):
                continue
            
            # Check if the new position is a wall
            if grid[newRow][newCol] == '#':
                continue
            
            # Calculate the tentative distance
            newDist = dist + 1
            
            # Update if the new distance is shorter than the known distance
            if newDist < distances[newRow][newCol]:
                distances[newRow][newCol] = newDist
                heapq.heappush(heap, (newDist, newRow, newCol))
    
    # Reconstruct the path
    if distances[goal_row][goal_col] == float('inf'):
        return []
    
    path = []
    currentRow, currentCol = goal_row, goal_col
    while (currentRow, currentCol) != (start_row, start_col):
        path.insert(0, (currentRow, currentCol))
        for move in moves:
            newRow, newCol = currentRow + move[0], currentCol + move[1]
            
            if newDist := distances[currentRow][currentCol] == distances[newRow][newCol] + 1:
                currentRow, currentCol = newRow, newCol
                break
    
    path.insert(0, (start_row, start_col))
    
    return path

from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    # Convert grid to width x height 2D array
    height = len(grid)
    width = len(grid[0])
    grid = [list(row) for row in grid]

    # Check if start or goal cannot be reached
    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] != '.' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] != '.':
        return []

    # Define possible directions (up, down, left, right)
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]

    def is_valid_move(x, y):
        return 0 <= x < height and 0 <= y < width and grid[x][y] == '.'

    # Use a queue for BFS traversal
    queue = deque([(start, [start])])
    visited = set()

    while queue:
        (x, y), path = queue.popleft()
        if (x, y) == goal:
            return path

        visited.add((x, y))
        for dx, dy in directions:
            nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
            if is_valid_move(nx, ny) and (nx, ny) not in visited:
                queue.append(((nx, ny), path + [(nx, ny)]))

    # No path found
    return []

def find_path(grid, start, goal):
    """
    Breadth First Search
    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breadth-first_search
    """
    N = len(grid)
    M = len(grid[0])
    assert (0 <= start[0] < N) and (0 <= start[1] < M)
    assert (0 <= goal[0] < N) and (0 <= goal[1] < M)
    assert grid[start[0]][start[1]] == "."
    assert grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == "."

    directions = [
        (-1, 0),
        (1, 0),
        (0, -1),
        (0, 1),
    ]

    queue = [(start, [start])]
    visited = set(start)

    while len(queue) > 0:
        point, path = queue.pop(0)
        if point == goal:
            return path

        for direction in directions:
            if N > point[0] + direction[0] >= 0 and M > point[1] + direction[1] >= 0:
                new_point = point[0] + direction[0], point[1] + direction[1]
            else:
                continue
            if grid[new_point[0]][new_point[1]] == "#" or new_point in visited:
                continue
            else:

                queue.append((new_point, path + [new_point]))
                visited.add(new_point)

    return []


def solve(grid, start, goal):
    """
    Custom public facade
    """
    return find_path(grid, start, goal)

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    # Memoization dictionary
    visited = {}
    # Queue of nodes to visit, starting with the start node
    q = [(start, [start])]
    while q:
        (row, col), path = q.pop(0)

        visited[(row, col)] = True

def parse_grid(grid):
    n = len(grid)
    return [[True] + [c == '.' for c in row] + [True] for row in grid]
def neighbors(point):
    yield point[0] - 1, point[1]
    yield point[0] + 1, point[1]
    yield point[0], point[1] - 1
    yield point[0], point[1] + 1
# DFS with a stack
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    grid = parse_grid(grid)
    n, m = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    row, col = start
    stack = [[(row, col), []]]
    while stack:
        (row, col), path = stack.pop()
        if (row, col) == goal:
            return path + [(row, col)]
        for (r, c) in neighbors((row, col)):
            if 0 <= r < n and 0 <= c < m and grid[r][c]:
                grid[r][c] = False
                stack.append([(r, c), [(row, col)] + path])
    return []

from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    def is_valid(row, col):
        return 0 <= row < len(grid) and 0 <= col < len(grid[0]) and grid[row][col] == '.'

    def get_neighbors(row, col):
        return [(row-1, col), (row+1, col), (row, col-1), (row, col+1)]

    def bfs(start, goal):
        queue = deque([(start, [])])
        visited = set([start])

        while queue:
            (row, col), path = queue.popleft()
            if (row, col) == goal:
                return path + [(row, col)]

            for (r, c) in get_neighbors(row, col):
                if (r, c) not in visited and is_valid(r, c):
                    visited.add((r, c))
                    queue.append(((r, c), path + [(row, col)]))

        return []

    path = bfs(start, goal)
    return path

	- recursive stacks are small (30^2 = 900)

	walk_coefs: list[dict] = [dict(l=-1, j=0), dict(l=1, j=0), dict(l=0, j=-1), dict(l=0, j=1)]
	walk: dict[tuple[int, int]] = dict()

	def walk_to(parent_cell: tuple[int, int] | None, goal_cell: tuple[int, int], canVisit) -> bool:
		row, column = parent_cell
		marked_cells: list[tuple[int, int]] = []

		for coef in walk_coefs:
			neighbour_row: int = row + coef['l']
			neighbour_column: int = column + coef['j']

			try:
				# no visiting used cells
				walk[neighbour_cell]
			except:
				walk[neighbour_cell] = walk[parent_cell] + 1

		if len(marked_cells) == 0:

            current_positions = [start]
            while current_positions:

                        queue.remove((next_position, [next_position]))
                        break

        for move in moves:
            next_row, next_col = curr_row + move[0], curr_col + move[1]
            if 0 <= next_row < rows and 0 <= next_col < cols and grid[next_row][next_col] == '.' and (next_row, next_col) not in visited:

                queue.append(((next_row, next_col), new_path))

"""
  When we are looking for the shortest path between two nodes in a graph,
  we can use BFS (breadth-first search). By working level-by-level, each node
  will be popped from the queue in the iteration in which its first time created
  (from a path). If this node is not the goal and doens't have a path in the queue, its path will be increased by 1 and
  soon will be qapped again during he next iteration as it should belong to the next level. Hence, the node when we 
  first see it in the queue has minimal viable path. 
  """
  # 1. Declarie the queue and set of visited nodes.
  # The set represents so that we can find a node in O(1) time.
  q, visited = [], set()
  # 2. Add the initial path (start, path from start to start, 0 steps) to the queue.
  # We use 'make_path' function to create a path from node in the queue, so we also
  # add the path from start to start and where the path only consists of a single node(node, node, 0)
  q.append(make_path(start, start, 0))
  visited.add(start)
  # While the set is not empty
  while q:
    # Pop the first node which will have minimal viable path (as the first time it seen in the queue)
    n, _, steps = q.pop(0)
    # If this n is the goal, we return the path (n, steps)
    if n == goal:
      path = make_path_from_steps(n, steps)
      return path
    # Otherwise we explore all paths from n and push them in the queue
    for neighbour in neighbours(n, grid):
      # If neighbour hasn't been seen, we explore the path from to neighbour (e.g. (n, neighbour)) and push it to the queue.
      if neighbour not in visited:
        visited.add(neighbour)
        q.append((neighbour, n, steps+1))
    print(f"n: {n}, queue: {q}")
  # Otherwise the path can't be found
  return []

def neighbours(n: tuple[int, int], grid: list[str]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
  # We can check up, down, left and right cells of n, 
  # but we also should make sure these cells are still in the grid
  neighbors = [["right", 1, 0], ["left", -1, 0], ["up", 0, 1], ["down", 0, -1]]
  rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
  possible_neighbours = []
  for direction, row, col in neighbors:
    r, c= n[0] + row, n[1] + col
    if r >= 0 and r < rows and c >= 0 and c < cols:
      possible_neighbours.append((r, c))
  return possible_neighbours


def make_path(n: tuple[int, int], prev: tuple[int, int], steps: int) -> tuple[tuple[int, int], tuple[int, int], int]:
  # Make path from by duplicating the previous path (node, prev, steps) 
  # and append the current path node to the duplicated. 
  return (n, next(make_path(prev, None, steps), n), steps)

  # We know the number of steps needed to n. 
  # We can assign each step of the path to an int value (e.g. we don't care actually which order of nodes 
  # are in the path). We push n whenever the steps are used up. 
  path = []
  while steps:
    path.append(0)
    steps -= 1
  path.append(1) #1 represents n

def solve(grid: list[str], start: tuple[int, int], goal: tuple[int, int]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """
    Solves the problem starting from start position moves right to left, top to bottom till the
    goal position is found.
    Finds the possible moves by looking at the neighbours of each node.
    From each neigbour node it recurses to find the path further.
    Once the path to the goal is found, the path is traced back from each node by checking their parents.
    
    Time complexity (worst case): O(rows * cols^3)
    Space complexity: O(cols)
    """
    rows, cols = (len(grid), len(grid[0]))

    class Node:
        """
        Node class for DFS.
        Visitates neighbours of any given node and pushes all the solution unique paths enclosing the goal into list_of_paths.
        """

        def __init__(self, row, col):
            self.row = row
            self.col = col
            self.parent = None
            self.unvisted_neighbours = set()

        def get_neighbours(self):
            """
            helper method that finds the valid neighbours if present for given node.
            """
            neighbours = set()
            for row_move, col_move in [(-1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (0, -1)]:
                new_row, new_col = (self.row + row_move, self.col + col_move)
                if new_row >= 0 and new_row < rows and (new_col >= 0) and (new_col < cols) and (grid[new_row][new_col] != '#'):
                    neighbours.add((new_row, new_col))
            assert len(neighbours) != 0
            return neighbours

        def discover(self, list_of_nodes, start, goal):
            """
            DFS. Finds the valid paths for the given node by visiting all nodes of each path
            until it reaches the goal. Keeps track of visited nodes to only visit nodes once.
            Returns a valid path to goal that it finds or an empty list.
            """
            if self not in list_of_nodes:
                return []
            if self == goal:
                path = []
                node = self
                while node:
                    path.append((node.row, node.col))
                    if node.parent == start:
                        path.append((start[0], start[1]))
                    node = node.parent
                path.reverse()
                return path
            self.parent = list_of_nodes[0]
            for neighbour in self.get_neighbours():
                if self in list_of_nodes:
                    list_of_nodes.remove(self)
                list_of_nodes.append(Node(*neighbour))
                result = self.discover(list_of_nodes, start, goal)
                if result:
                    return result
            if list_of_nodes[-1] != self:
                return []
            return []
    path = []
    head = Node(*start)
    for row in range(rows - 1, -1, -1):
        for col in range(cols - 1, -1, -1):
            if (row, col) == goal:
                path = head.discover([head], head, goal)
                return path
            elif grid[row][col] != '#':
                list_of_nodes = [Node(row, col)]
                head = list_of_nodes[0]
                for neighbour in list_of_nodes[0].get_neighbours():
                    list_of_nodes.append(Node(*neighbour))
                path = head.discover(list_of_nodes, head, goal)
                if path:
                    return path
            list_of_nodes.append(Node(row, col))
    return path

# Breadcrumb labyrinth https://www.redblobgames.com/pathfinding/a-star/introduction.html

    UNDISCOVERED = object()

    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    nodes: dict[tuple[int, int], Breadcrumb | object] = dict()
    start_breadcrumb = Breadcrumb(value=1, came_from=start)
    nodes[start] = start_breadcrumb
    goal_breadcrumb = Breadcrumb(value=UNDISCOVERED, came_from=goal)

    frontier = {start}
    while frontier and nodes[goal] is UNDISCOVERED:

        new_frontier = set()
        for cell_pos in frontier:
            if nodes[cell_pos].value is UNDISCOVERED:
                raise ValueError(f"Dead lock - start position is U in {cell_pos}")
            cell_val = nodes[cell_pos].value
            cell_breadcrumb = nodes[cell_pos]

            for row_delta, col_delta in ((0, 1), (1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, -1)):
                row, col = cell_breadcrumb.came_from
                new_r, new_c = row + row_delta, col + col_delta
                # We do not need to check for walls as we are already inside grid limits.
                if (
                    0 <= new_r < rows
                    and 0 <= new_c < cols
                    and grid[new_r][new_c] == "."
                    and nodes.get((new_r, new_c), UNDISCOVERED) is UNDISCOVERED
                ):
                    frontier_next = Breadcrumb(value=cell_val + 1, came_from=(new_r, new_c))
                    nodes[new_r, new_c] = frontier_next
                    new_frontier.add((new_r, new_c))
                    if new_frontier is goal_breadcrumb:
                        break

        frontier = new_frontier

    if nodes[goal] is UNDISCOVERED:
        return []

    path = []  # type: list[tuple[int, int]]
    cell = goal
    while cell is not start:
        path.append(cell)
        cell = nodes[cell].came_from

    return path[::-1]


class Breadcrumb:
    """Запрятанная лестница"""
    value: int
    came_from: tuple[int, int]

    def __init__(self, value: int, came_from: tuple[int, int]):
        self.value = value

    def __repr__(self):
        return str({

    # find the length of the grid
    n: int= len(grid)
    m: int= len(grid[0])

    # define a function to check if a cell is free
    def is_free(cell: tuple[int, int]) -> bool:
        return cell[0] >= 0 and cell[0] < n and cell[1] >= 0 and cell[1] < m and grid[cell[0]][cell[1]] == '.'

    # define a function to find the adjacent free cells
    def find_adjacent_free_cells(cell: tuple[int, int]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
        adjacent_cells: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
        if is_free((cell[0] - 1, cell[1])):
            adjacent_cells.append((cell[0] - 1, cell[1]))
        if is_free((cell[0] + 1, cell[1])):
            adjacent_cells.append((cell[0] + 1, cell[1]))
        if is_free((cell[0], cell[1] - 1)):
            adjacent_cells.append((cell[0], cell[1] - 1))
        if is_free((cell[0], cell[1] + 1)):
            adjacent_cells.append((cell[0], cell[1] + 1))
        return adjacent_cells
    
    # define a function to check if the goal is reached
    def goal_reached(cell: tuple[int, int]) -> bool:
        return cell == goal

    # define a function to find the path
    def find_path() -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
        # initialize the queue with the start cell
        queue: list[tuple[int, int]] = [start]
        # create a dictionary to store the parent of each cell
        parent: dict[tuple[int, int], tuple[int, int]] = {}
        parent[start] = None
        # keep a record of the visited cells
        visited: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
        while queue:
            # remove the first element from the queue
            current_cell: tuple[int, int] = queue.pop(0)
            # check if the goal is reached
            if goal_reached(current_cell):
                # initialize an empty list to store the path
                path: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
                # iterate through the dictionary until the start cell is found
                while current_cell != start:
                    # append the current cell to the path
                    path.append(current_cell)
                    # set the current cell as the parent cell
                    current_cell = parent[current_cell]
                # return the reversed path and the visited cells
                return path[::-1], visited | {current_cell}
            # iterate through the adjacent free cells
            for adjacent_cell in find_adjacent_free_cells(current_cell):
                # check if the adjacent cell is not visited
                if adjacent_cell not in visited:
                    # add the adjacent cell to the queue
                    queue.append(adjacent_cell)
                    # set the parent of the adjacent cell
                    parent[adjacent_cell] = current_cell
                    # mark the adjacent cell as visited
                    visited.add(adjacent_cell)
        # return an empty list if the goal is not reached
        return [], visited

    # return the path and the visited cells
    return find_path()

maxRow = len(grid)-1
    maxCol = len(grid[0])-1

    def bfs():
        nonlocal grid, start, goal, maxRow, maxCol
        queue = [(start[0], start[1], [], start)]
        visited = set()
        while len(queue) > 0:
            (row, col, path, parent) = queue[0]

            if (row, col) == goal:
                return path

            if (row, col) in visited:
                queue.pop(0)
                continue

            visited.add((row, col))

            neighbors = []
            if row > 0 and grid[row-1][col] != "#": #Move to Top
                neighbors.append((row-1, col))
            if row < maxRow and grid[row+1][col] != "#": #Move to Bottom
                neighbors.append((row+1, col))
            if col > 0 and grid[row][col-1] != "#": #Move to Left
                neighbors.append((row, col-1))
            if col < maxCol and grid[row][col+1] != "#": #Move to Right
                neighbors.append((row, col+1))

            for neighbor in neighbors:
                queue.append((neighbor[0], neighbor[1], path+(parent, neighbor), neighbor))

            queue.pop(0)

        return []

    return bfs()

    if not grid or not grid[0]:
        return []

from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    # 获取网格的行数和列数

    # BFS队列，存储 (row, col, path)
    queue = deque()
    queue.append((start[0], start[1], [start]))

    visited = set()
    visited.add((start[0], start[1]))
    
    while queue:
        r, c, path = queue.popleft()

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0]) if rows > 0 else 0

    # Directions: up, down, left, right
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]

    queue = deque()
    queue.append((start[0], start[1], [start]))  # (row, col, path)
    visited = set()

        # Check if goal is reached
        if (r, c) == goal:
            return path

        # Explore neighbors
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            if is_valid(nr, nc) and (nr, nc) not in visited:

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    from collections import deque

    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])

    # Directions: up, left, down, right
    directions = [(-1, 0), (0, -1), (1, 0), (0, 1)]

    queue = deque()

                visited[nr][nc] = True
                new_path = path + [(nr, nc)]
                queue.append((nr, nc, new_path))

    """
    Find a valid path from start to goal in the grid using BFS.

class Solution:
    def solve(self, grid, start, goal):
        from collections import deque
        
        rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
        directions = [(0,1), (1,0), (0,-1), (-1,0)]  # right, down, left, up
        
        # Check if start or goal are out of bounds or not free

            return []
        if not (0 <= goal[0] < rows and 0 <= goal[1] < cols and grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '.'):
            return []
        
        # BFS setup
        queue = deque()
        queue.append((start[0], start[1], [start]))
        visited = set()
        visited.add((start[0], start[1]))
        
        while queue:
            r, c, path = queue.popleft()
            
            # Check if current cell is the goal
            if (r, c) == goal:
                return path
            
            # Explore neighbors
            for dr, dc in directions:
                nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
                if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols and grid[nr][nc] == '.' and (nr, nc) not in visited:
                    visited.add((nr, nc))
                    queue.append((nr, nc, path + [(nr, nc)]))
        
        # Goal not reached
        return []

class Solution:
    def solve(self, grid, start, goal):
        from collections import deque
        
        rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
        directions = [(0,1), (1,0), (0,-1), (-1,0)]  # right, down, left, up
        
        # Check if start or goal are out of bounds or not free
        if not (0 <= start[0] < rows and 0 <= start[1] < cols and grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '.'):
            return []
        if not (0 <= goal[0] < rows and 0 <= goal[1] < cols and grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '.'):
            return []
        
        # BFS setup
        queue = deque()
        queue.append((start[0], start[1], [start]))
        visited = set()
        visited.add((start[0], start[1]))
        
        while queue:
            r, c, path = queue.popleft()
            
            # Check if current cell is the goal
            if (r, c) == goal:
                return path
            
            # Explore neighbors
            for dr, dc in directions:
                nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
                if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols and grid[nr][nc] == '.' and (nr, nc) not in visited:
                    visited.add((nr, nc))
                    queue.append((nr, nc, path + [(nr, nc)]))
        
        # If goal not reached
        return []

# Solving the Maze Problem with BFS

```python
from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    # Get grid dimensions
    rows = len(grid)
    if rows == 0:
        return []
    cols = len(grid[0])
    
    # Check if start or goal is out of bounds or is a wall
    if (not (0 <= start[0] < rows and 0 <= start[1] < cols) or 
        grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or 
        not (0 <= goal[0] < rows and 0 <= goal[1] < cols) or 
        grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#'):
        return []
    
    # Directions: up, down, left, right
    directions = [(-1,0), (1,0), (0,-1), (0,1)]
    
    # BFS setup
    queue = deque()
    queue.append((start[0], start[1], [start]))
    visited = set()
    visited.add((start[0], start[1]))
    
    while queue:
        r, c, path = queue.popleft()
        
        # Check if we reached the goal
        if (r, c) == goal:
            return path
        
        # Explore neighbors
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols:
                if grid[nr][nc] == '.' and (nr, nc) not in visited:
                    visited.add((nr, nc))
                    queue.append((nr, nc, path + [(nr, nc)]))
    
    # If we exhaust the queue without finding the goal
    return []

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    if rows == 0:
        return []
    cols = len(grid[0])
    
    # Directions: up, down, left, right
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    
    # Priority queue: (cost, row, col, path)
    pq = [(0, start[0], start[1], [start])]
    visited = set()
    visited.add((start[0], start[1]))
    
    while pq:
        cost, r, c, path = heapq.heappop(pq)
        
        # Check if goal is reached
        if (r, c) == goal:
            return path
        
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols:
                if grid[nr][nc] == '.' and (nr, nc) not in visited:
                    visited.add((nr, nc))
                    new_path = path + [(nr, nc)]
                    heapq.heappush(pq, (cost + 1, nr, nc, new_path))
    
    # Goal not reachable
    return []

import heapq

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    if rows == 0:
        return []
    cols = len(grid[0])
    
    # Directions: up, down, left, right
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    
    # Priority queue for Dijkstra's algorithm
    pq = []
    heapq.heappush(pq, (0, start))
    
    # Keep track of visited cells and their distances
    visited = {start: 0}
    path = {}
    
    while pq:
        dist, current = heapq.heappop(pq)
        
        # If we reached the goal, reconstruct the path
        if current == goal:
            # Reconstruct path from goal to start
            path_list = []
            while current in path:
                path_list.append(current)
                current = path[current]
            path_list.append(start)
            path_list.reverse()
            return path_list
        
        # Explore neighbors
        for dr, dc in directions:
            r, c = current
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            
            # Check if the new position is within grid boundaries
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols:
                # Check if cell is free
                if grid[nr][nc] == '.':
                    new_dist = dist + 1
                    neighbor = (nr, nc)
                    
                    # If neighbor hasn't been visited or found a shorter path
                    if neighbor not in visited or new_dist < visited[neighbor]:
                        visited[neighbor] = new_dist
                        path[neighbor] = current
                        heapq.heappush(pq, (new_dist, neighbor))
    
    # If goal is unreachable
    return []

```python
from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    # Directions: up, right, down, left
    directions = [(-1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (0, -1)]
    rows = len(grid)
    if rows == 0:
        return []
    cols = len(grid[0])
    
    # Check if start or goal is out of bounds or is a wall
    if (start[0] < 0 or start[0] >= rows or start[1] < 0 or 
        start[1] >= cols or grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#'):
        return []
    if (goal[0] < 0 or goal[0] >= rows or goal[1] < 0 or 
        goal[1] >= cols or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#'):
        return []
    
    # BFS setup
    queue = deque()
    queue.append((start[0], start[1], [start]))
    visited = set()
    visited.add((start[0], start[1]))
    
    while queue:
        r, c, path = queue.popleft()
        
        # Check if we reached the goal
        if (r, c) == goal:
            return path
        
        # Explore neighbors
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols:
                if grid[nr][nc] == '.' and (nr, nc) not in visited:
                    visited.add((nr, nc))
                    new_path = path + [(nr, nc)]
                    queue.append((nr, nc, new_path))
    
    # Goal not reachable
    return []

# Solution using BFS to find a path in a grid
from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    # Get grid dimensions
    rows = len(grid)
    if rows == 0:
        return []
    cols = len(grid[0])
    
    # Directions: up, down, left, right
    directions = [(-1,0), (1,0), (0,-1), (0,1)]
    
    # Check if start or goal is out of bounds or not free
    if (start[0] < 0 or start[0] >= rows or 
        start[1] < 0 or start[1] >= cols or 
        grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#'):
        return []
    
    if (goal[0] < 0 or goal[0] >= rows or 
        goal[1] < 0 or goal[1] >= cols or 
        grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#'):
        return []
    
    # BFS setup
    queue = deque()
    queue.append((start[0], start[1], [start]))
    
    # Visited set to avoid cycles
    visited = set()
    visited.add((start[0], start[1]))
    
    while queue:
        r, c, path = queue.popleft()
        
        # Check if we reached the goal
        if (r, c) == goal:
            return path
        
        # Explore neighbors
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols:
                if grid[nr][nc] == '.' and (nr, nc) not in visited:
                    visited.add((nr, nc))
                    queue.append((nr, nc, path + [(nr, nc)]))
    
    # Goal not reachable
    return []

To solve this problem, we need to find a valid path from a start cell to a goal cell in a grid, where the grid consists of free cells ('.') and walls ('#'). We can use a breadth-first search (BFS) algorithm to explore the grid and find the shortest path.
